mainTopic: The ruling on an engaged woman's extra כתובה money, when the closeness of marriage begins (חופה or ביאה), and רבי יהודה's view on a bride's receipt and on giving up part of the כתובה.
overview: The גמרא concludes that both sides of the argument about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rely on reading the husband's intent. One side says the extra כתובה money was pledged for the marriage itself, so an engaged woman does not collect it. The other side says it was pledged out of a closeness that already existed, so she does. After a list of conflicting rulings, including רב נחמן's curse on judges who follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the הלכה is fixed like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רבין then asks whether the closeness of the חופה alone earns the extra money, or only the closeness of ביאה. A ברייתא about 'the first night' turns out to fit both views. רב אשי asks about a bride who became a נידה under the חופה, and his question ends in תיקו. The גמרא next asks how רבי יהודה can let a bride write a receipt when elsewhere he rejects receipts; רבי ירמיה and אביי each give an answer. Finally, the גמרא asks why a spoken waiver of the כתובה does not work for רבי יהודה. It answers that the חכמים strengthened the rabbinic כתובה, and then challenges that answer from the husband's rabbinic right to פירות.

steps.title: Both opinions rely on assessing intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier attempt to split the two opinions over אומדנא. It concludes that both sides use אומדנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both of them follow an assessment of the person's intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up its earlier idea that only one side relies on guessing the husband's intent. It says both sides do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא assumed the argument about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was really an argument about whether we use אומדנא at all. That broke down once it became clear that both רב and רבי נתן do use אומדנא. So the argument must be about how to read the husband's intent, not whether to read it.

keyTerms.meaning: An estimate of a person's intent based on the circumstances

phrases.english: Rather: both of them follow the assessment of intent.
phrases.notes: "Both" means רב and רבי נתן from just before this: the one who rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the one who doesn't.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one side ignores the husband's intent. Both sides are trying to read his mind. They only disagree about what he was thinking.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier approach on the daf, which tied the dispute to whether one uses אומדנא at all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the dispute: both sides use the same principle but apply it differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the opinion that rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה relies on אומדנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both opinions rely on אומדנא and differ only in how they read the husband's intent.

steps.title: How each side reads the husband's intent
steps.stepSummary: The view that follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה clearly fits אומדנא. The opposing view also uses אומדנא: the husband pledged the extra money out of closeness, and that closeness already existed during the engagement.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the one who says the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, this works well. For the one who says it does not, this too is an assessment of intent. He pledged the extra money because of the closeness between them, and that closeness already exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side uses אומדנא. One side says the husband wrote the extra amount for the wedding. The other side says he wrote it because they were already close, so an engaged woman collects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view is a simple reading of intent: he pledged the extra money only so that the marriage would happen. The other side guesses a different motive, a feeling of closeness. Since that closeness was already there during the engagement, his reason for the pledge already came true and she collects.

keyTerms.meaning: An assessment of the person's mind or intent
Closeness of minds; a feeling of intimacy and affection

phrases.english: The one who says the halakha follows him — that is fine,
The one who says the halakha does not follow him —
here too it is an assessment of intent.
It was because of closeness of minds,
phrases.notes: "It" means the husband's pledge of the extra amount.

phrases.english: and indeed that closeness has already come about.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read the husband's mind. One says he pledged the extra money for the wedding, so an engaged woman doesn't get it. The other says he pledged it out of closeness, which already existed, so she does.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה — שַׁפִּיר, מַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reframing from step 1 for each side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows how the opposing view is also an אומדנא, just with a different motive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruling against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would mean ignoring the husband's intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ruling against him assumes the motive was closeness, which already existed during the engagement.

steps.title: רבי ינאי rejects רב חנינא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא says the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רבי ינאי sends him out and rules that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא sat before רבי ינאי and said: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רבי ינאי said to him: Go out, read your verses outside! The הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from explaining the opinions to stating rulings. It tells a short story in which רבי ינאי strongly rejects ruling like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנינא was known for his skill with פסוקים. רבי ינאי tells him that his strength is פסוקים, not deciding הלכה. This gives a clear ruling against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, so an engaged woman would collect the extra amount.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
phrases.english: Rav Chanina sat before Rabbi Yannai

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: and said: The halakha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
He said to him: Go out,
read your verses outside!
phrases.notes: Stick to פסוקים, which you're good at, and don't decide הלכה here.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: The halakha does not follow Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from explaining the reasoning to listing rulings on the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי: the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבינו rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי, quoting רבינו (רבי יהודה הנשיא), rules that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said in the name of our teacher: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that disagrees with רבי ינאי. It comes from רבי יהודה הנשיא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי ינאי rejected this ruling so sharply, an important authority supports it. So the ruling רב חנינא gave was not baseless.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teacher, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling opposite to רבי ינאי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה הנשיא: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: שמואל also rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting שמואל, also rules that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second authority, שמואל, who rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two major authorities support ruling like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, against רבי ינאי. By that ruling, an engaged woman who is widowed or divorced does not collect the extra amount, because it was pledged for the wedding.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ינאי rules against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רבי יהודה הנשיא and שמואל both rule like him.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second authority to support the ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רב נחמן's own view disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, speaking for himself, rules that the הלכה does NOT follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן himself said: The הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after quoting שמואל in favor of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the גמרא tells us that רב נחמן's own personal view goes the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רב נחמן was only passing along שמואל's ruling. Here we learn his own opinion, which is the opposite. So the list of rulings is now split.

keyTerms.meaning: His own (speaking for himself, not quoting a teacher)
The law does not follow (this view)

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman himself said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: The halacha is not like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רב נחמן's personal view against the ruling he quoted from שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב נחמן's own name: the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרדעא quote רב נחמן the other way
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא report that רב נחמן ruled that the הלכה DOES follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the scholars of נהרדעא say in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: A different tradition about רב נחמן says he actually ruled in favor of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two reports of what רב נחמן held, and they contradict each other. This sets up the גמרא's need to give a clear final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the town נהרדעא in Babylonia

phrases.english: And the scholars of Neharde'a say in the name of Rav Nachman:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite report of רב נחמן's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the scholars of נהרדעא, רב נחמן held that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Even despite רב נחמן's curse, the law follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: Even though רב נחמן cursed any judge who ruled like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the הלכה still follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though רב נחמן cursed and said, 'Any judge who rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, such-and-such should happen to him,' even so, the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that רב נחמן felt strongly enough against this view to curse judges who followed it. Still, it rules that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse shows how strongly רב נחמן opposed this view. But the גמרא does not let that strong feeling decide the law. The ruling stands with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Such-and-such should happen to him' (an unnamed misfortune)

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָט רַב נַחְמָן וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: And even though Rav Nachman cursed and said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל דַּיָּינָא דְּדָאֵין כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Any judge who rules like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
such-and-such should happen to him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: even so, the halacha is like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָט רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the conflicting reports by ruling in favor of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Despite רב נחמן's strong opposition, the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The practical ruling follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the הלכה למעשה, the actual practice, follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the practical הלכה is like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion with a ruling for real-life cases: follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After so many opinions going back and forth, the גמרא makes clear this is how judges should actually rule. In practice, a woman widowed or divorced after only אירוסין gets the basic כתובה but not the extra amount her husband added.
steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The extra כתובה money was pledged for the marriage itself, so a woman who was only engaged does not collect it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up רבין's next question: exactly when does that marriage closeness begin?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלָכָה לְמַעֲשֶׂה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: And the practical halacha is like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ruling into a firm practical decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבין asks: does the חופה alone bring the closeness?
steps.stepSummary: רבין asks about a bride who entered the חופה but had no ביאה. Is it the closeness of the חופה or the closeness of ביאה that earns the extra money?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין asked: If she entered the חופה but had no relations, what is the law? Does the closeness of the חופה earn it, or does the closeness of ביאה earn it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the extra money depends on marital closeness, רבין asks exactly when that closeness starts: at the חופה, or only at ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know an engaged woman does not get the extra money. The case in between is a woman who had a חופה but no ביאה. If the חופה's closeness counts, she collects. If only ביאה counts, she is treated like an engaged woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (a real question that needs an answer)
The wedding canopy, the stage that completes the marriage
Earns it here (makes her entitled to the extra money)

steps.confusionAlert: 'קוֹנָה' here does not mean 'acquires the woman.' It means: which closeness earns her the extra כתובה money that was promised because of that closeness.

phrases.english: Ravin asked:
If she entered the chuppah but had no relations, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means she was then widowed or divorced. Does she get the extra money?

phrases.english: Does the closeness of the chuppah earn it,
or does the closeness of relations earn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the final ruling to ask when the closeness actually begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the closeness of the חופה alone, or only the closeness of ביאה, entitles her to the extra כתובה money.

steps.title: Proof from 'the closeness of the first night'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught by רב יוסף says the extra money was written for the closeness of 'the first night.' That fits the חופה, which happens once, better than ביאה, which keeps happening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יוסף taught that he wrote it for her only because of the closeness of the first night. If you say the closeness of the חופה earns it, that explains 'the first night.' But if you say the closeness of ביאה earns it, is there ביאה only on the first night and never again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer רבין. It argues that the words 'first night' point to the חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חופה is a one-time event at the start of the marriage, so 'first night' fits it well. ביאה continues all through the marriage, so tying it to just the first night sounds odd. That suggests the closeness of the חופה is what counts.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Yosef taught:
He wrote it for her only
because of the closeness of the first night.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חִיבַּת חוּפָּה קוֹנָה —
phrases.english: It makes sense if you say the closeness of the chuppah earns it:
that is why it says 'the first night.'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ חִיבַּת בִּיאָה קוֹנָה,
phrases.english: But if you say the closeness of relations earns it,
are there relations only on the first night,
and from then on there are none?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבין's question from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the closeness of the חופה earns the extra כתובה money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא: the extra money was written 'only because of the closeness of the first night.'

steps.title: But a חופה isn't only at night either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: a חופה can also happen by day, so 'night' does not fit the חופה perfectly either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, then, the חופה? Is a חופה only at night and not by day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. If 'night' is meant exactly, it doesn't match the חופה, since a חופה can take place during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof relied on how exact the phrase 'first night' is. But the word 'night' is a problem for the חופה reading too. So the phrase cannot be read so exactly, and the proof gets weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: But what, then? (pushing back on the other side)

phrases.english: But what, then, the chuppah?
phrases.notes: He means: is the phrase really talking about the חופה?

phrases.english: Is a chuppah only at night and not by day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof by showing that 'night' doesn't fit the חופה reading either.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from 'first night' that the closeness of the חופה earns the extra money.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חופה is not limited to night, so the exact wording does not really point to the חופה.

steps.title: By that logic, relations aren't only at night either
steps.stepSummary: The other side answers back: ביאה is also allowed by day in a dark house, as רבא said. So 'night' doesn't fit ביאה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, is ביאה only at night and not by day? But רבא said that if it was in a dark house, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question around. If 'night' must be exact, it doesn't fit ביאה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא allows relations in the daytime in a dark house. So ביאה is not limited to night either. The word 'night' now seems to cause trouble for both readings.

keyTerms.meaning: And by your reasoning (turning the argument back on the asker)

phrases.english: And by your reasoning:
are relations only at night and not by day?
But Rava said:
If it was in a dark house, it is permitted!
phrases.notes: Relations by day are normally not allowed, but a dark house makes it permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing the 'night' problem also hits the ביאה reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'first night' refers to ביאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on רבא, ביאה is permitted by day in a dark house, so it is not limited to night either.

steps.title: 'Night' just describes the usual practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that for ביאה, 'night' is not a strict rule. It just reflects the normal way of doing things.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: it teaches us proper conduct, that relations are at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why mentioning 'night' is no problem for the ביאה reading. It simply describes what usually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though ביאה is allowed by day in a dark house, the normal practice is at night. So the ברייתא's word 'night' fits ביאה as a description, not as a limit. The day-versus-night problem is removed from the ביאה reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper or normal conduct, the usual way of doing things

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying daytime relations are forbidden. רבא already allowed them in a dark house. 'Night' just describes what normally happens.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
it teaches us proper conduct,
that relations are at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: אוֹרַח אַרְעָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection that ביאה can also happen by day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording as describing normal practice, not a strict limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'night' in the ברייתא is a problem for the ביאה reading, since ביאה is permitted by day in a dark house.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'night' just reflects the normal practice of ביאה at night, so it fits the ביאה reading.

steps.title: The 'night' wording fits the חופה view too
steps.stepSummary: Now that 'night' has been explained for ביאה, the גמרא asks whether it still causes trouble for the חופה view. It answers no: an ordinary חופה leads to ביאה, so 'night' just describes the normal practice. The ברייתא therefore proves nothing either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: So is the 'חופה' view difficult? No, it is not difficult either. A normal חופה is meant to lead to ביאה, so the ברייתא is only teaching the usual way: it happens at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the חופה side is still in trouble, and answers that it is not. 'Night' works for both sides, so the proof from the ברייתא falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 the חופה view was attacked because a חופה can happen by day. Now the same answer used for ביאה in Step 14 is used for חופה: a plain חופה is meant to lead to ביאה, which normally happens at night. Since both readings survive, רבין's question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: the normal way of the world, usual practice
it is difficult, it is a problem

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about 'the first night' fits both views. It cannot settle whether the extra money comes from the closeness of חופה or of ביאה.

phrases.english: Then is the 'wedding canopy' view difficult?
phrases.notes: He means the problem raised in Step 12: a חופה can also happen by day.

phrases.english: The canopy view is also not difficult:
since an ordinary canopy is meant to lead to intercourse,
it is teaching us the normal way of doing things,
that it happens at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חוּפָּה קַשְׁיָא? חוּפָּה נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'normal practice' answer from Step 14 to defend the חופה view against the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording as describing normal practice, not as a strict rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a חופה can happen by day, the word 'night' seemed to rule out the חופה view.
steps.terutzMaskana: A typical חופה leads to ביאה at night, so 'night' fits the חופה view too. The ברייתא proves nothing.

steps.title: What if the bride became a נידה under the חופה?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks a question that builds on רבין's. If the closeness of חופה earns the extra money, does that only apply to a חופה where ביאה is possible? What about a bride who became a נידה, so ביאה was not allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if she entered the חופה and became a נידה, what is the law? Even if you say the closeness of the חופה earns the money, maybe that is only a חופה fit for ביאה, and not one where ביאה is forbidden. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question that grows out of רבין's question. He wants to know whether a חופה where ביאה is forbidden still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי grants for the sake of argument that the closeness of the חופה is what counts. He then asks whether that closeness depends on ביאה being possible. A bride who is a נידה cannot be with her husband, so maybe that חופה has less closeness and does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (a real question to be resolved)
she became a נידה, her period began
if you will conclude, even if you say
or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If she entered the canopy and her period began, what is the law?
Even if you will say
that the closeness of the canopy earns it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the extra money of the כתובה from רבין's question.

phrases.english: that may be a canopy that is fit for intercourse,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוּפָּה דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְבִיאָה — לָא,
phrases.english: but a canopy that is not fit for intercourse does not,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבין's question and asks about a further case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the closeness of the חופה earn the extra money even when ביאה is forbidden because the bride is a נידה?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle רב אשי's question, so it is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב אשי's question with תיקו, meaning no answer was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found that decides whether a חופה where ביאה is forbidden still earns the extra money. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand, the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no.' It means the גמרא found no answer either way.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a חופה where the bride became a נידה earns the extra money remains an open question.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new part of the משנה. There, רבי יהודה says the husband may write the full amount for a בתולה, and she writes a receipt as if she already got part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if he wants, he writes for a בתולה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up its next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה lets the husband write the full 200 for a בתולה. She then writes 'I received a מנה from you,' as if he already paid half. This step only quotes the line; the challenge comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he wishes, he writes for a virgin, and so on.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: he writes her a document for two hundred, and she writes, 'I received a מנה from you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רָצָה, כּוֹתֵב לִבְתוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה lets the husband write the full כתובה for a בתולה while she writes a receipt for part of it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה elsewhere rejects receipts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי יהודה really allow a receipt? In another משנה, about a borrower who paid part of his debt, רבי יהודה says to swap in a new loan document. It is רבי יוסי who says to write a receipt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that we write a receipt? But we learned: if someone paid part of his debt, רבי יהודה says he should swap the document, and רבי יוסי says he should write him a receipt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה by pointing to another משנה, where רבי יהודה seems to be against writing receipts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the debt case, רבי יהודה does not want a separate receipt. He wants the old document replaced with a new one for the amount still owed, probably because a receipt has to be guarded forever. In our משנה he lets the bride write a receipt, so his two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn in a משנה

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that we write a receipt?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
One who repaid part of his debt:
Rabbi Yehuda says: he should exchange it.
phrases.notes: He swaps the old loan document for a new one that lists only what is still owed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: יִכְתּוֹב לוֹ שׁוֹבָר!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he should write him a receipt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּכוֹתְבִין שׁוֹבָר? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's ruling just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the bride may write a receipt for part of her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In בבא בתרא, רבי יהודה rejects receipts for partly paid debts and requires a new document. That seems to contradict his allowing a receipt here.

steps.title: The receipt is written inside the כתובה itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that in our משנה the receipt is written inside the כתובה itself. Since there is no separate receipt to guard, רבי יהודה's concern does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: this is when her receipt is written inside the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה settles the contradiction. He explains that our משנה is about a receipt written on the כתובה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה objects to a separate receipt, which the payer would have to keep safe. Here the bride's receipt is written right into the כתובה document, so there is no separate paper to lose. That is why רבי יהודה allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: when her receipt is inside it (inside the כתובה)
the אמורא who gives this answer

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not contradict himself. He objects only to a separate receipt, while in our משנה the receipt is written inside the כתובה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is when her receipt is inside it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כתובה. The receipt is written right on the כתובה, so there is no separate paper to keep safe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is about a specific kind of receipt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bride writes a separate receipt, which רבי יהודה should reject.
steps.terutzMaskana: The receipt is written within the כתובה itself, so רבי יהודה's concern about separate receipts does not apply.

steps.title: אביי: A receipt here is different because no money was really paid
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the contradiction in רבי יהודה differently. Even with a separate receipt, the worry from the loan case does not apply to a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if the receipt is not written inside the כתובה, there is still no problem. With a loan, the borrower really paid. If he loses the receipt, the lender could bring out the loan document and collect again. Here, did the husband really give her anything? She only said it to him. If he keeps the receipt, good. If he does not keep it, he is the one who caused his own loss.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer to the question from step 19, different from רבי ירמיה's answer in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the loan case the money was really paid, so losing the receipt would cause an unfair loss to an innocent borrower. In the כתובה case the husband paid nothing; the receipt is only her way of giving up part of the money. If he is careless and loses it, the loss is his own fault, so רבי יהודה does not mind a receipt here.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing that part of a debt was paid
He caused a loss to himself

steps.confusionAlert: In the loan case, the person who would be hurt is the borrower, who really paid. In the כתובה case, the only person who could lose is the husband, who paid nothing. That is why the two cases are different.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if you say it is a case where her receipt is not written inside it,
phrases.notes: "Inside it" means inside the כתובה document itself, like רבי ירמיה said in step 20.

phrases.english: granted, there, he certainly paid him,
phrases.notes: "There" is the loan case from step 19, where the borrower paid part of his debt.

phrases.english: so perhaps the receipt will get lost,
and the lender will take out the loan document,
and collect again a second time.
Here, did he certainly give her anything?
It is merely something she said to him,
if he kept it safe, he kept it safe;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא נַטְרֵיהּ — אִיהוּ הוּא דְּאַפְסֵיד אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: if he did not keep it safe, he is the one who caused a loss to himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 19, offered instead of רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה rejects receipts for loans, he should also reject a separate receipt for a כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's worry is about someone who really paid being harmed. In a כתובה nothing was paid, so a separate receipt is fine.

steps.title: Why did רבי ירמיה not answer like אביי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why אביי did not answer like רבי ירמיה, but asks why רבי ירמיה did not answer like אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand why אביי did not answer like רבי ירמיה: the משנה does not say the receipt is written inside the כתובה. But why did רבי ירמיה not answer like אביי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers and asks what pushed רבי ירמיה to his narrower reading. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reason for avoiding רבי ירמיה's answer is clear: the משנה never mentions a receipt inside the כתובה. אביי's answer seems simpler and fits the plain words of the משנה, so the גמרא wants to know why רבי ירמיה did not use it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable that... (sets up a contrast with what is not understood)
It does not teach / the text does not say

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אַבָּיֵי לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה,
phrases.english: Granted, Abaye did not say like Rabbi Yirmeya,
because the משנה does not teach that her receipt is inside it.
But Rabbi Yirmeya, what is the reason
that he did not say like Abaye?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אַבָּיֵי לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 20 and 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ירמיה limited the משנה to a receipt written inside the כתובה instead of using אביי's reasoning.

steps.title: A decree so this receipt is treated like ordinary receipts
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה holds that the רבנן made a גזירה: a receipt for a כתובה is treated like any other receipt, so people do not mix them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the receipt here is forbidden because of receipts in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 22: רבי ירמיה agrees there is no real danger here, but holds there is a גזירה anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה accepts that in a כתובה case the danger is small. Still, a separate receipt looks just like a normal loan receipt, so the רבנן forbade it so people would not start using receipts in loan cases. Only a receipt written inside the כתובה avoids this, because it is clearly different.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a separate receipt for a כתובה is fine, since nothing was really paid. רבי ירמיה: only a receipt inside the כתובה works, because of a גזירה made because of ordinary receipts.

phrases.english: It is a decree: the receipt here is forbidden
because of the ordinary receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שׁוֹבָר דְּהָכָא אַטּוּ שׁוֹבָר דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ירמיה holds there is a גזירה treating a separate כתובה receipt like an ordinary receipt, so only a receipt inside the כתובה is allowed.

steps.title: Only a written receipt works, not just saying it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out what the משנה implies: the wife gives up part of her כתובה only because she wrote a receipt. Just saying so would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it works is that she wrote it for him. But if she only said it, it would not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the wording of רבי יהודה in the משנה. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה needed a written receipt for the wife to give up part of her כתובה. That suggests a spoken waiver alone would not work, even for רבי יהודה. The גמרא will now ask why not.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... (used to infer that otherwise the law would be different)

phrases.english: The reason is that she wrote it for him,
but if only spoken, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּכָתְבָה לֵיהּ אֲבָל עַל פֶּה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the receipt question to what the משנה implies about a spoken waiver.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, a wife gives up part of her כתובה only with a written receipt, not with words alone.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה says a condition about money stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 24. רבי יהודה holds that a condition about money takes effect, so a spoken waiver should work too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? It is a money matter, and we have heard that רבי יהודה said: in a money matter, his condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that only a written receipt works, using another ruling of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is about money. רבי יהודה elsewhere says that conditions about money are valid even if they change what the תורה would normally give. So a wife's spoken waiver of part of her כתובה should be valid too, without any receipt.

keyTerms.meaning: His condition stands; it takes effect

phrases.english: Why? It is a money matter,
and we have heard that Rabbi Yehuda said:
in a money matter, his condition stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that, for רבי יהודה, a spoken waiver of the כתובה does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה holds that conditions about money take effect. A כתובה is money, so a spoken waiver should work.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a condition to give up food and clothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's view. A man makes קידושין on condition the woman gives up food, clothing and marital relations. רבי מאיר says the condition is void; רבי יהודה says it stands for money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If a man says to a woman, "You are married to me on condition that you have no claim on me for food, clothing and marital relations," she is married and his condition is void. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: in a money matter, his condition stands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the challenge in step 25, showing where רבי יהודה said a money condition stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and clothing are money matters that the תורה requires a husband to give. Still, רבי יהודה lets the couple agree to cancel them. If so, a wife should be able to give up part of her כתובה just by saying so. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, clothing and marital relations: what a husband owes his wife

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה only says the condition stands for the money items (food and clothing), not for עונה, which is not about money.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who says to a woman,
"You are hereby married to me
on condition that you have no claim on me
for food, clothing and marital relations,"
she is married, and his condition is void;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
in a money matter, his condition stands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds a condition about money takes effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא קידושין) about קידושין on condition that the woman gives up food, clothing and marital relations.

steps.title: A כתובה is rabbinic, so the Sages made it stronger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a כתובה is דרבנן, and the חכמים strengthened their own laws more than Torah laws. So a spoken waiver cannot reduce a כתובה, but it can work for food and clothing, which come from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that a כתובה is a rabbinic law. The Sages gave their own laws more strength than Torah laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 25-26. It explains why רבי יהודה lets a spoken condition work for food and clothing but needs a written receipt for the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and clothing are Torah obligations about money, so a condition about them works even when only spoken. The כתובה is rabbinic. The חכמים protected it more strongly, so the wife can only give part of it up through a written receipt.

keyTerms.meaning: The כתובה is a rabbinic obligation, not a Torah one
Reinforcement; extra strength given to a law
To their own words, meaning the Sages' own laws

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that a rabbinic law is stronger than a Torah law. The idea is that the Sages worried people would treat their laws lightly, so they protected them with extra rules.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the marriage contract is rabbinic,
and the Sages made reinforcement for their own words
more than for those of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 25-26 by separating rabbinic rights from Torah rights.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a Torah obligation and a rabbinic obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a spoken money condition works for food and clothing, it should also work to reduce a כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה is rabbinic and has extra protection, so only a written receipt can reduce it. Food and clothing are Torah obligations and need no such protection.

steps.title: The husband's right to produce is also rabbinic but was not strengthened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the husband's right to eat the produce of his wife's property is also rabbinic, yet the רבנן did not give it extra strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the husband's right to the produce is rabbinic, and the Rabbis did not strengthen it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 27. It points to another rabbinic law that did not get extra strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule were that every rabbinic law gets extra strength, then פירות should also be protected. The גמרא claims that פירות were not strengthened, so the rule from step 27 looks wrong. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce; here, the husband's right to eat the produce of his wife's property
But look; it opens a challenge

phrases.english: But produce is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: This means the husband's right to eat the produce of his wife's property, which comes from the Rabbis.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis did not make reinforcement for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי פֵּירוֹת דְּרַבָּנַן, וְלָא עֲבַדוּ לְהוּ רַבָּנַן חִיזּוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle offered in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 27 that the חכמים strengthened rabbinic laws more than Torah laws
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פירות are rabbinic but did not get extra strength, so being rabbinic does not by itself bring extra protection.

steps.title: The משנה about produce of produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves its challenge from a משנה. רבי יהודה says the husband still eats the produce of the produce until he writes that he has no claim to her property, its produce, or the produce of its produce, forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, he always eats the produce of the produce until he writes to her: 'I have no claim at all to your property, its produce, or the produce of its produce, forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove the claim in step 28. It shows that the husband's rabbinic right to produce can be given up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the husband can fully give up his rabbinic right to פירות. No extra protection stops him. This seems to go against step 27, which said rabbinic rights get extra strength.

keyTerms.meaning: The produce of the produce; income from property bought with the first produce
I have no claim or dispute; a formula for giving up rights

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question the גמרא must answer next: why the כתובה is strengthened but the husband's right to פירות is not.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in the מסכת, on דף 83a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the קשיא in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן did not give the husband's rabbinic right to פירות extra strength
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה (כתובות 83a): רבי יהודה says the husband eats the produce of the produce until he writes that he gives it all up
